name: Sydney
departure_points: Mosman Bay wharf / The Spit / Roseville Bridge ramp
Cronulla public wharf, Tonkin St (Port Hacking)

species_seasons.when: Year-round in Sydney Harbour; peak September to December
Best October to July in the harbour
Year-round on the offshore reefs; winter is strong for reef fish
Summer (around the FADs); larger fish early in the season
Summer, often from November-December; caught in every month
From about Christmas on inshore reefs and estuary mouths
February to May, peaking late summer-early autumn
Late summer through winter, best in winter (with albacore)

notes: Sydney Harbour itself holds kingfish to over a metre and big jewfish within sight of the Opera House; harbour guides fish east of the bridge, North Harbour and Middle Harbour.
Offshore reef trips typically fish 1-12 nautical miles out in 30-120 m of water for snapper, morwong, pearl perch, flathead and nannygai.
Named sport and game grounds include Long Reef, the 9-mile and 12-mile reefs, 'the Peak' and the NSW DPI fish aggregating devices (FADs).
Southern trips from Cronulla run past Jibbon Bommie and along the Royal National Park coast; Port Botany gives quick access to the southern reefs.
Winter brings gemfish runs at Browns Mountain with mako and blue sharks, and occasional southern bluefin in July-August.

name: Central Coast
departure_points: Hardys Bay jetty (Killcare Rd, Broken Bay)

species_seasons.when: Year-round reef fishing
Seasonal game fishing (tag and release preferred)
Summer pelagic

notes: Terrigal boats launch from The Haven and are offshore within minutes; reef species include snapper, jewfish, kingfish, teraglin, blue morwong, flathead, trevally and John Dory.
Hardys Bay gives access to the offshore reefs and wrecks of the Bouddi Peninsula, with calm-water options inside Broken Bay and the Hawkesbury when it is windy.
At least one Terrigal operator runs fishing charters only in summer (December to April).

name: Newcastle
departure_points: Other public jetties on Lake Macquarie by arrangement

species_seasons.when: Year-round
Year-round, with twilight sessions aimed at mulloway
Cooler months in Swansea Channel

notes: Lake Macquarie is a Recreational Fishing Haven of about 110 sq km - the largest coastal saltwater lake in Australia - linked to the sea by the Swansea Channel.
Swansea Channel is popular for dusky flathead, bream, whiting and luderick; Australian salmon school there in the cooler months, and yellowtail kingfish are a prized catch around Swansea Bridge.
The lake has a series of DPI artificial reefs built with Recreational Fishing Trust funds.
Flathead, bream and whiting are the lake's 'big three'; mulloway and kingfish are the prized sportfish.
The Hunter River and Newcastle Harbour (oyster beds, wrecks and structure) are also fished by local guides.

name: Port Stephens

species_seasons.when: Late spring through summer (30-100 kg fish); December to March at the FADs and the Big Gibber
December to March, often in packs on bait balls
January to March over the continental shelf
April to July wide of Port Stephens
December to March around the FADs
Reef trips around Broughton, Cabbage Tree and Little islands

notes: Port Stephens is one of the few places where blue, black and striped marlin can all be caught in a single day, and it hosts the NSW Interclub game fishing tournament.
Named grounds: Broughton Island, Cabbage Tree Island, Boondelbah, Little Island, Fingal Head, the Big Gibber, 'the Car Park' and the FAD region about 20 km out.
Inside the port, the estuary and its Myall, Karuah and Tilligerry tributaries hold flathead, bream, whiting, mulloway, luderick, kingfish and even longtail tuna.

name: Port Macquarie
departure_points: Town Green boardwalk, Short St car park end (74 Clarence St)
McInherney Park boat ramp (River Park Rd), Hastings River

species_seasons.when: Year-round (dusky flathead in the estuaries)
Year-round in the Hastings River
October to April on the sand flats
Warmer offshore months
Offshore reefs; spring and summer are the main seasons

notes: Offshore boats leave from the town centre and fish the reefs for snapper, pearl perch, kingfish and jewfish.
The Hastings River is tidal for about 32 km inland; the Maria River, Limeburners Creek and the Camden Haven, Manning and Macleay rivers are also fished.
Australian bass are guided from September to May in the Hastings, Maria and Macleay rivers (catch and release).

name: South West Rocks
departure_points: South West Rocks boat shed moorings
New Entrance Rd, South West Rocks

species_seasons.when: Winter and spring are best
Winter and spring
Summer (with spotted and school mackerel)
Summer surface fishing, with sailfish, wahoo and mahi mahi

notes: The first ocean reef is about ten minutes from the bar and only a kilometre offshore; most fishing is 1-5 km out in 10-100 m of water, ranging to about 30 km.
The continental shelf is only about 12 nautical miles off South West Rocks, so the East Australian Current pushes warm water close in; three deep canyons along the shelf hold blue marlin.
When it is rough outside, the Macleay River estuary offers flathead, trevally, bream, whiting, mulloway and mangrove jack.

name: Coffs Harbour

species_seasons.when: Year-round reef fishing
Summer offshore pelagic season
Summer, out on the shelf

notes: The Solitary Islands Marine Park is the oldest marine park in NSW, covering about 71,000 ha and 100 km of coast from Coffs Harbour to the Sandon River; tropical and temperate currents meet here.
Charter reef trips fish live- and dead-bait reefs from about 20 m to 120 m for snapper, pearl perch, tuskfish and jewfish; South Solitary Island is a noted kingfish, cobia, mackerel and wahoo spot.
Check marine park zoning (FishSmart app) before fishing.

name: Yamba & Iluka
departure_points: Yamba Shores Tavern, The Mainbrace (Yamba Marina area)

species_seasons.when: Offshore reefs
Offshore reefs
Seasonal pelagic

notes: Charter grounds run from Evans Head in the north to Sandon in the south and out to the continental shelf; many reef trips fish 5-10 km off the Clarence River bar.
Operators also run humpback whale watching in season between Woody Head and Angourie.

name: Ballina & Byron Bay

species_seasons.when: Year-round; specialty in about 80 m of water ~30 km off Evans Head
Reef target off Byron and Brunswick

notes: A new DPI offshore artificial reef (two steel towers in 32 m, about 5 km south of the Richmond River mouth) was deployed off Ballina in March 2026; expected species are mackerel, snapper and mulloway.
Brunswick Heads boats fish off Byron Bay and the Cape Byron Marine Park area for snapper, pearl perch, jewfish and kingfish, with mackerel, wahoo, tuna and marlin in the warmer months.

name: Tweed Heads
departure_points: Tweed Marina, River Terrace, Tweed Heads

species_seasons.when: Year-round reef fishing
December to March game season (with wahoo, mackerel, mahi mahi and tuna)

notes: The closest reefs are within 3 km of the Tweed River entrance, extending east to the continental shelf; live baiting targets kingfish, cobia, mulloway, amberjack and samsonfish.
Humpback whales are commonly seen on winter fishing trips.

name: Wollongong

species_seasons.when: Year-round reef fishing
December to April (black, striped and blue)
December to April and June to October (with bluefin and albacore in winter)

notes: Wollongong boats drift the coast between Stanwell Park and Shellharbour, from just off the beach to about ten miles out (Bellambi, Five Islands/Port Kembla).
From Kiama the boat is 'outside' almost immediately; reef trips stay within about 15 km in up to 140 m, and the shelf is about 30 km offshore.
Deep-sea trips for blue-eye trevalla, gemfish and hapuku are a cool-season option, roughly May to September, in water to 400 m.

name: Jervis Bay & Shoalhaven

species_seasons.when: Jervis Bay is renowned for squid over the seagrass edges
Excellent bottom fishing offshore and in the bay

notes: Deep water sits right next to Jervis Bay and the continental shelf is close, so offshore trolling and jigging for kingfish, tuna, bonito, salmon and dolphinfish is easily reached.
Jervis Bay's land-based game fishing is legendary, with several record marlin landed from the ledges.
The bay is a marine park: check the zoning map and FishSmart app; spearfishing is banned in creeks and sanctuary zones.

name: Batemans Bay & Narooma
departure_points: d'Albora Marina, Beach Rd, Batemans Bay

species_seasons.when: Reef and island target
Offshore from Bermagui

notes: Batemans Bay boats fish the reefs of the bay and the Tollgate Islands for snapper, kingfish, morwong, pigfish and flathead.
Narooma's town wharf is the closest port to Barunguba Montague Island, a key reef and game fishing area.
Bermagui operators offer reef, kingfish, tuna and deep-water trips (gemfish, blue-eye trevalla).

name: Merimbula & Eden

species_seasons.when: Main game season November to end of July (with yellowfin, albacore and striped tuna, shark and broadbill)
Year-round on the inshore reefs ('Snapper country')
Wide reef trips February to April (with ocean perch and shark)
About November to June south of Eden (most 5-8 kg)

notes: Eden has the Southern Hemisphere's third-deepest natural harbour, with no bar to cross.
Merimbula's artificial reef has been in place since September 2018.

name: Lord Howe Island

species_seasons.when: Year-round; winter is best
Offshore
Offshore

notes: The island sits on the world's southernmost coral reef; the East Australian Current pushes deep water up its slopes, so tropical and temperate species overlap.
Kingfish here are huge; the marine park also holds some of NSW's biggest silver trevally, plus emperors, jobfish and cods on the bottom.
Balls Pyramid, the world's tallest sea stack (552 m), is about 23 km from the island and is a premier offshore destination.
Lagoon sight-casting 'grand slam': trevally, silver drummer, bluefish and the endemic double header wrasse. Spearfishing is banned in the marine park; bag limits apply to bluefish and double header.
